key_insight: LLM agents can translate natural-language household preferences into reliable home energy schedules, achieving near-MILP performance when paired with native tool calling and live energy data.
engineering_relevance: This points to a practical control interface for home energy management that can lower costs, improve demand-response participation, and simplify multi-appliance optimization.
method: Tool-calling ReAct agent for scheduling flexible loads
Uses live Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, PV estimates, usage data, and a retrieval-augmented knowledge base
Benchmarked against MILP ground truth across tariff, constraint-conflict, solar co-optimization, and week-long deployment scenarios
evidence_signal: Across three commercial LLMs, native function calling gave 100% scheduling success and 96.7–98.0% of oracle savings over a simulated week, with text-parsed actions performing much less reliably.
watch_item: Results depend on accurate external inputs and stable tool integration, so real-world deployment may be sensitive to forecast errors, data availability, and malformed action parsing.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
